title: API & Webhook Automation

body.text: Connecting systems is one of Codex's strengths:
writing API endpoints, webhook handlers, and integrations with external services
— attach the API docs of the service you're connecting to, then describe the behavior you want.

example: "Write a webhook handler that receives the 'payment.succeeded' event from Stripe and updates the order status to paid, verifying the signature"

title: Resilient integrations

body.text: A good integration must handle failures:
— always specify in the instruction 'what to do if the downstream API fails,' because networks can always fail.

example: "Add 3 retries with exponential backoff; if a webhook is duplicated, ignore it (idempotent); and log every request"

question: Before having Codex connect an external API, what should you attach?
What should a good webhook handler have?
Why define behavior for when the downstream API fails?

options.text: Because networks can always fail — the system must handle it

question: How do you design a resilient API/webhook integration?

options.text: Handle errors and retries, and validate inputs and outputs
